newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends up on institutional support.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends up on institutional support.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mostly up on Friday on institutional support despite overnight losses on the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The most active February 1997 contract ended at 19,550 yuan ($2,355) per tonne, rising 50 yuan. It opened at 19,350 yuan, hitting an intra-day low of 19,310 and a high of 19,560.
November fell 40 to 18,950, December rose 90 to 19,300, January 90 to 19,530, March 60 to 19,560, April 40 to 19,560, May dropped 20 to 19,500.
Combined volume fell to 45,680 tonnes from 87,760.
Copper opened lower but institutional and other speculative buying pushed most contracts to or near their intra-day highs.
Traders said overnight LME losses made copper open lower but institutions built many long positions at low levels, giving confidence to many retail investors.
"Institutional support pushed most contracts above the 19,500-yuan level, indicating that they are optimistic about the future trend," one trader said.
"But copper cannot rise sharply due to over-surplus of spot copper," he said.
Traders said long and short position holders were divided about future market trends, with the result that contracts have moved around 19,500 yuan over the past few days.
"Technical charts on the LME support a further rise of copper despite poor fundamentals, which gave confidence to long position holders in Shanghai," a second trader said.
The November contract will begin delivery next Monday. Its last open interest was 5,902 lots, against October's 4,070. One lot is five tonnes.
Analysts expect copper to move around the 19,500-yuan in the next few days.
In aluminium, there was only trading of 1,000 tonnes of the November contract, which ended at 13,400 yuan per tonne, losing 50 yuan.
